name: Pasta alla Trapanese
steps: Wash and dry the tomatoes and basil. Core and roughly chop the tomatoes, keeping their juice. Lightly toast the blanched almonds in a dry pan for 3–4 minutes until fragrant, then cool. Peel the garlic and grate the vegetarian hard cheese.

Crush the almonds and garlic to a coarse crumb in a mortar or food processor. Add basil and pulse briefly, then add the fresh tomatoes, their juice, 5 g salt and black pepper. Add the olive oil gradually and pulse only until a rustic, spoonable raw pesto forms; do not cook it or turn it completely smooth.

Bring the measured water to a rolling boil, add the remaining 4 g salt and busiate, and stir to separate the twists. Cook according to the pack, usually 10–13 minutes, until tender with a slight bite and no dry centre. Reserve 150 ml cooking water, then drain.

In a large bowl off the heat, toss the hot pasta with the raw tomato-almond pesto and half the grated cheese. Add reserved cooking water a spoonful at a time until the pesto lightly coats the twists; the sauce should stay fresh and textured, not watery.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Divide into four warm bowls, scatter over the remaining vegetarian cheese and a few basil leaves, and serve immediately.
tips: Fresh ripe tomatoes, almonds and basil distinguish this Trapani pesto from concentrated sun-dried tomato pesto. Busiate is traditional; if unavailable, use another eggless short twisted pasta.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
